summary: The note describes inclusivity policies adopted after September 1, 2023 to improve minority representation in local government, centered on the Representation and Inclusivity in Governance Act (RIGA). It covers baseline data showing underrepresentation, early outcomes such as more minority candidates and higher turnout, and challenges like official attrition and campaign financing. It also covers youth programs, community organizations, and media coverage rules, and stresses that progress is ongoing.
one_line: Overview of post-2023 inclusivity policies, especially RIGA, aimed at increasing minority representation in local government, with outcomes, challenges, and supporting initiatives.
key_facts: An October 10, 2023 study by the Local Governance Research Consortium (LGRC) found only 14% of elected local officials were from minority groups, though these groups make up 40% of the general population.
State Representative Marisol Vargas and City Councilor Jamal Adeel led the drafting of the policies.
The Representation and Inclusivity in Governance Act (RIGA) was signed into law on December 5, 2023.

RIGA requires demographic audits, development plans for underrepresentation, implicit bias awareness training, community outreach to encourage minority candidacies, and monitoring and reporting of progress.
An LGRC interim report published September 15, 2024 showed a 5% increase in minority candidates running for local government seats.
The demographic audits revealed under-representation in advisory committees and commissions, which began to be rectified through outreach and appointments.
The February 2025 report "Hurdles to Inclusivity," commissioned by the Department of Local Affairs, documented an 18% attrition rate among minority officials after election.
The City of Arboridge reported a 30% participation increase in its Civic Leadership Development Program (CLDP) since its inception in April 2024.
The League of United Cultural Heritage (LUCH) and similar groups moved from advocacy to active partnership with local governments, identifying potential minority leaders.
Voter turnout in predominantly minority precincts increased by 3.7%, helped by civic education, easier voting access, early voting and mail-in ballots.
New Harbor's municipal council enacted the Election Equity Fund, which as of July 2025 has disbursed over $500,000 in grants to qualifying minority candidates.
The Inclusive Media Representation Act (IMRA) mandates fair coverage of all candidates regardless of race or ethnicity; media monitoring bodies have reviewed coverage since January 2026.
